questions.answer:
What it tests: Whether you use the last thirty seconds well. Most candidates waste them.
A strong answer contains: One thing, prepared in advance, that did not come up naturally: a piece of evidence for your candidacy, a correction to something you fumbled earlier, or genuine interest with a reason attached. Thirty seconds, then stop.
Red flags: No, I think we covered everything. It is a free shot and you declined it. Also using it to repeat something you already said.

questions.question: What EBITDA would be high GAAP or IFRS
questions.answer: IFRS EBITDA since leases are capitalized which means that leases are considered depreciation expense as opposed to an operating expense which is added back to EBITDA

questions.answer: I would prefer $100 in AR since a short cash cycle allows for quick cash conversion and there are no carrying costs with AR as opposed to inventory which incur storage costs.

A company has a Net Debt / EBITDA of 10x and sells off a positive-EBITDA generating business for 5x EV / EBITDA. What happens to the Net Debt / EBITDA ratio?
questions.answer: The whole company prior to the divestiture has an EV / EBITDA of >10x. While the payback of debt with cash will reduce net debt, the divesture’s sale at a lower valuation means more EBITDA was given up relative to the sale value than the average of the entire firm. As a result, EBITDA declines by more than net debt, and the ratio increases.

You acquire a business for $1000 cash that has $1000 F.A, $800 L; impact on BS
questions.answer:
The Book Value of the company is $200 ($1000 F.A. - $800 L) which leads to Goodwill of $800 since we paid $1000 for the company
Assets: Cash goes down by $1000, F.A. up by $1000, Goodwill up by $800 so net change to assets is up by $800 Liabilities & Shareholder’s Equity: Liabilities up by $800 Therefore, both sides balance being up by $800
